# porch_automation_token (Resource)

An automation token (`porch_at_…`) for another integration, issued by the provider's own token (ADR-0048). Without `tenant` it is an installation token with a `role`: `admin`, `auditor` (installation health and audit log) or `inspector` (reads the configuration of every tenant, changes nothing). With `tenant` it is a tenant token holding `permissions` in that tenant, for example `["app:read", "service_account:read"]`.

The provider's token must be an installation `admin` token created by an installation owner (to issue installation or tenant tokens), or a tenant token holding a write permission (to issue narrower tokens of its tenant). The new token is no broader than the provider's token and cannot outlive it; revoking the provider's token revokes it too. Every argument forces a new token. The secret is returned only at creation and kept in state (sensitive); an expired or revoked token disappears from state, so the next apply issues a new one. Destroying the resource revokes the token and every token it issued. Import with `installation/<id>` or `<tenant>/<id>` (the secret stays unknown).

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The provider's token must be an installation admin token created by an installation owner.

# Reads the configuration of every tenant and changes nothing (for example a catalogue or monitoring connector).
resource "porch_automation_token" "inspector" {
  name            = "deed"
  role            = "inspector"
  expires_in_days = 180
}

# Reads one tenant's applications and service accounts.
resource "porch_automation_token" "smith_apps" {
  name            = "smith-apps-reader"
  tenant          = porch_tenant.smiths.id
  permissions     = ["app:read", "service_account:read"]
  expires_in_days = 90
}

output "inspector_token" {
  value     = porch_automation_token.inspector.token
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Display name. Changing it forces a new token.

### Optional

- `expires_in_days` (Number) Lifetime in days (1–366); it may not outlive the provider's token. Required unless `never_expires` is set. Changing it forces a new token.
- `never_expires` (Boolean) Issue an installation token that never expires (ADR-0046). Needs a provider token that never expires itself. Default `false`. Changing it forces a new token.
- `permissions` (Set of String) Tenant permissions (`<resource_type>:<action>`), 1–50. Required with `tenant`. Changing them forces a new token.
- `role` (String) Installation token role: `admin`, `auditor` or `inspector`. Required without `tenant`. Changing it forces a new token.
- `tenant` (String) ID or slug of the tenant for a tenant token; omit for an installation token. Changing it forces a new token.

### Read-Only

- `expires_at` (String) When the token expires (RFC 3339); empty when it never expires.
- `hint` (String) Last characters of the token, as shown in the admin UI.
- `id` (String) Token ID (`atk_…`).
- `issued_by` (String) ID of the token that issued this one (the provider's token at creation).
- `token` (String, Sensitive) The token secret, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Only known after create; unknown after import.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import porch_automation_token.inspector installation/<token_id>   # the secret stays unknown
terraform import porch_automation_token.smith_apps <tenant>/<token_id>
```
